answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before taking jobs, then randomly select agents and pay only for work verified by independent peers. Splitting one operator into many identities does not multiply influence unless they also provide more stake; colluding reviewers risk losing theirs. The fable of free identities meets a beacon of auditable selection, though capital costs can exclude honest newcomers. Shale-hard security still depends on reviewers resisting capture.
